intro.en: Chiropractic care for back pain, neck pain, headaches and sports injuries. Find where it hurts, see what we would do, and book a time that fits.

announcement.en: New patients: exam + first adjustment $95 · same-week appointments

text.en: Desk stiffness usually starts in the neck and upper back. A few adjustments plus hourly breaks and a raised screen help most people within weeks.
Pain running below the knee can come from an irritated nerve in the low back. We test nerve function on the first visit before choosing treatment.
Sudden low back pain after lifting is common and usually settles. Keep walking gently; avoid bed rest.
Tension headaches often come from tight neck and shoulder muscles. If a headache is sudden and severe, see a doctor first.

label.en: Hurts when I run or train

text.en: Training pain often comes from how the hip, knee and shoulder move together. We look at the whole chain, not just the sore spot.
Low back and pelvic pain are common in the second and third trimester. We use side-lying and pillow techniques only.
Aching or sharp pain across the low back, often after lifting, long drives or sitting.
Pain, tingling or numbness from the buttock down one leg.
Stiffness and pain from looking down at screens; hard to check blind spots.
A band of pressure around the head or behind the eyes, worse late in the day.
Knots between the shoulder blades, burning after long computer work.
Pinching pain lifting the arm overhead, common in swimmers, climbers and lifters.
Pain around the kneecap or outer hip that builds with mileage.
Low back and pelvic pain as the bump grows; trouble rolling over in bed.

notes.en:
Numbness in the groin, or loss of bladder or bowel control: go to the emergency room now
Sudden weakness in an arm or leg
Back pain with fever, or weight loss you cannot explain
A fall, car crash or hard hit in the last few days
The worst headache of your life, or a headache with a stiff neck and fever

text.en: A short health history online, so the visit is spent on you, not paperwork.
Where it hurts, what makes it worse, and movement, strength and nerve tests.
What we think is going on, how many visits it usually takes, and what it costs.
If it is safe to start, a gentle adjustment and soft-tissue work the same day.
Two or three exercises sent to your phone with photos.
Mild soreness is normal. Walk gently, drink water, and use heat or ice for 15 minutes if it helps.
Stand up every 45 minutes; roll the shoulders back and tuck the chin for 10 seconds.
Do your two home exercises once a day. Stop any that make pain spread down a limb.
Add a 20-minute walk most days. Sleep on your side with a pillow between the knees.
Call us the same day. Go to the ER for any of the warning signs listed above.

us.en: We give you a superbill for HSA/FSA and out-of-network claims; many plans cover chiropractic. We are not in-network with Medicare.

ca.en: Visiting from BC? You pay in USD at the clinic; prices in CAD are estimates. Our receipts work with most extended health benefit plans.

text.en: Clicked "pain down one leg", saw sciatica and booked decompression the same week. Eight visits later I sleep through the night.
Drove down from Surrey. The receipt went straight through my extended health plan.
Gentle with my 30-week bump and the home exercises helped. Saturday slots fill fast.

a.en: No. You can book directly. If your insurance needs a referral for reimbursement, ask your doctor and bring it to the first visit.
Most people feel pressure and sometimes a pop, not pain. We use gentler techniques if you prefer, and we never adjust without your OK.

q.en: How many visits will I need?

a.en: Each condition card shows a usual range. We give you a plan after the first exam and recheck every few visits; if you are not improving, we refer you on.
Only when the exam suggests a need, such as after a fall. We refer you to imaging nearby rather than X-ray everyone.
Comfortable clothes you can move in, like leggings or sweatpants and a T-shirt.

Recheck, adjustment and a short stretch for the area we are working on.
Hands-on work for tight muscles in the neck, shoulders and back; pairs well with an adjustment.
A motorised table gently stretches the low back or neck to ease disc and nerve pain.
Assessment, joint work and a home exercise plan for runners, lifters and weekend players.
Gentle techniques and a pregnancy pillow table for low back and pelvic pain.

Ten follow-up adjustments to use within 5 months.
